title: China Buys US Wheat/Sorghum + Tech Stocks Crash on Data Center Fears (with guest Matt Bennett)

bullets: Treasuries rallied on the tech sell-off. Yields fell as much as 12 bp, the lowest since early September, and 10Y futures are up 5 straight weeks
The 10Y yield is 4.83%, down from a 5.3% peak earlier this year. Joe thinks the Treasury bear market that began in 2020 may be bottoming
Markets still mostly expect a 25 bp Fed hike in December, but some are now betting on no change. Lower crude has eased inflation worries
Farm operating loans run about 7% (7.5–8% at the high end). An Illinois program offers about 5–5.5%
Nasdaq fell 5.5–6.3% (the video gave both figures), about 15% below its all-time high. S&P fell 4.4% and the Dow 3.4%, the worst day since April 2025
The trigger was fear that Democratic midterm wins bring curbs on AI and data centers; about 40% of planned US data-center capacity is in states signaling a pause
This morning the Nasdaq is up 1.6% and the Dow down about 1%
Chinese buyers signed $600M of US sorghum and wheat purchase agreements in Shanghai (per Reuters)
China bought $7.2B of US farm goods other than soybeans from January to September, against a $17B annual commitment
China says it will buy more only if both sides implement the agreed tariff cuts
China has no US wheat on the books this year. Matt expects some corn buying eventually
Soybeans 54 mbu (−44% w/w), China the top buyer. Corn 51 mbu (+10% vs the 4-week average), Mexico the top buyer. Wheat 20 mbu, Philippines the top buyer
Year-to-date sales vs last year: corn −34%, wheat −28%, soybeans +76% (China has about 16 MMT booked)
They think USDA’s soybean export forecast is too low, maybe by 50+ mbu
Jan soybeans are down 9 straight sessions, −14¢ to about $11.88, a $1.50 drop from the $13.50 high in early September
The market seems to be pricing a StoneX-type yield of about 55 bu/acre, which adds about 160 mbu of supply; strong demand offsets it, and they estimate ending stocks of about 370 mbu, not 400+
Dec corn fell 4¢ to about $4.40 and is about $4.44 today. Minnesota corn yield: StoneX 207 vs USDA 195, and most growers think it’s a record
Wheat briefly broke its July low overnight. Matt expects winter wheat acres down at least 3M
Drought worsened in northern Indiana, southern Illinois and Missouri, and improved in Minnesota and the Plains
Share of area in drought: corn 19%, soybeans 28%, winter wheat 48%
Weekend wind flattened some unharvested corn. Central Illinois is too dry and warm for fall nitrogen application
It should stay mostly dry for 1–2 more weeks
Live cattle fell $2.40–3.60 and feeders $2.93–6.98. Futures keep following the cash market lower

flags: The Nasdaq figure was garbled (“5 a.5%”); Joe’s chart showed −6.3%
The Texas governor-elect was captioned “Gina Hinosa”, likely Hinojosa
The crude price was captioned “9092” and is unclear
Central Illinois rain was captioned “1500s”, probably about 0.15 inch
“Fed hike” is what they said, not a caption error
